title: Chicken thigh, baked, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh is the dark meat from the upper part of a bird's leg. When baked in the oven with a coating (breaded, sauced or marinated), it stays juicy while the crispy crust adds flavor and texture. The skin and coating are edible and often contain additional taste components.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark meat contains more iron and zinc than white meat.
Baking with a coating helps retain moisture, making the meat more tender.
Chicken thighs are used in many traditional dishes, from French confit to Asian teriyaki.
The skin provides beneficial fats but also contributes cholesterol.
When properly cooked, the skin becomes crunchy and aromatic, a favorite element in many recipes.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains vitamin B6, niacin and riboflavin, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Thigh meat supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Selenium and vitamin B6 help maintain a normal immune response.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Fats in the skin and coating provide a quick source of energy, especially during high physical activity.

items.title: High fat and cholesterol
items.content: Skin and coating increase saturated fat content, so people with cardiovascular disease should limit intake.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked meat may contain Salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: Breadings can contain dairy, gluten or nuts, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salty sauces and marinades can raise sodium levels, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked coated chicken thighs are convenient hot or cold—in salads, sandwiches or as a main dish. The skin and coating can be eaten together with the meat, adding crunch and flavor. Serve in bite‑size pieces for easy consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it keeps quality for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
